pinyin: tiān shàng yī rì, dì xià yī nián
literal: heaven · above · one · day, earth · below · one · year
natural: one day in heaven, a year on earth

meaning.en: Time runs much slower in heaven than on earth: a day among the gods equals a year among mortals.
meaning.zh: 天上的时间比人间慢得多：天上一天，相当于人间一年。

equivalents: a day in heaven is a year on earth
time moves differently among the gods

examples.zh: 神话里说天上一日，地下一年，所以神仙不觉得岁月长。
examples.en: Myth says a day in heaven is a year on earth, so the immortals don't feel time dragging.

examples.zh: 他在山里住了几天，回来才知道天上一日，地下一年，外面已翻天覆地。
examples.en: He spent a few days in the mountains and returned to find the world transformed, as if a day in heaven were a year on earth.

usage.en: A popular belief in Chinese fairy tales and in 《西游记》, where Sun Wukong's few days in Heaven correspond to years below. Also said 天上一天，地上一年 or 天上一日，人间一年; often used jokingly when time seems to pass quickly or strangely.
usage.zh: 中国神话传说和《西游记》中常见的说法，天上几日，人间已过数年。也说“天上一天，地上一年”“天上一日，人间一年”，常用于戏称时间过得飞快或错位。

synonyms: 山中方七日，世上已千年

text: 一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼
pinyin: yī nián sān bǎi liù shí rì, fēng dāo shuāng jiàn yán xiāng bī
literal: one · year · three · hundred · sixty · days, wind · knives · frost · swords · harshly · press upon
natural: all year round, knife-like winds and sword-like frost press hard upon me

meaning.en: All year round, a hostile environment attacks like wind and frost; a lament about a life of persecution and no shelter.
meaning.zh: 一年到头，恶劣的环境像风霜刀剑般逼迫着人；比喻处境艰难、受尽压迫。

equivalents: a life under constant harsh pressure
buffeted by cruel winds all year

examples.zh: 读到“一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼”，才明白黛玉寄人篱下的苦。
examples.en: Reading 'all year round, wind like knives and frost like swords bear down', I finally understood Daiyu's misery as a dependant.

examples.zh: 长期的职场压力让她想起“一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼”。
examples.en: The years of pressure at work reminded her of 'all year round the wind and frost press hard'.

origin.source: 曹雪芹《红楼梦》第二十七回《葬花吟》

story.en: In 'Song of Burying Flowers', Daiyu compares herself to fallen petals, helpless under a hostile climate.
story.zh: 林黛玉在《葬花吟》中以落花自比：“一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼。”

usage.en: Quoted for harsh circumstances, often with a literary touch. The next line is 明媚鲜妍能几时，一朝漂泊难寻觅。
usage.zh: 形容环境险恶、长期受压，书面感强。下句为“明媚鲜妍能几时，一朝漂泊难寻觅”。

pinyin: nǚ ér shì shuǐ zuò de gǔ ròu
literal: daughters · are · water · made · 's · flesh and bone

meaning.en: A saying of Jia Baoyu that young women are pure and clear like water, in contrast to men, who are made of mud.
meaning.zh: 贾宝玉的名言：女儿像水一样清澈纯洁，男子则像泥一样浑浊。

examples.zh: 宝玉说“女儿是水做的骨肉”，表达他对女孩子的珍惜。
examples.en: Baoyu says 'girls are made of water' to show how much he cherishes them.

examples.zh: 她动不动就哭，朋友打趣说女儿是水做的骨肉。
examples.en: She cries easily, so her friends joke that girls are made of water.

story.en: Jia Baoyu tells a friend: 'Girls are made of water, and men are made of mud; I feel fresh when I see girls and foul when I see men.'
story.zh: 贾宝玉说：“女儿是水做的骨肉，男人是泥做的骨肉。我见了女儿，我便清爽；见了男子，便觉浊臭逼人。”

usage.en: In modern speech it is often shortened to 女人是水做的 and used to describe tender, tearful women, sometimes teasingly. Keep in mind it is a character's romantic opinion in the novel.
usage.zh: 现代常说“女人是水做的”，形容女性温柔易落泪，有时含调侃。原是小说人物宝玉的看法。

text: 诸葛亮借东风——巧借天时
pinyin: zhū gě liàng jiè dōng fēng —— qiǎo jiè tiān shí
literal: Zhuge Liang · borrow · east · wind — cleverly · borrow · heaven's · timing
natural: Zhuge Liang borrows the east wind

meaning.en: Zhuge Liang 'borrowed' the east wind for the fire attack; to use a favourable moment or condition skilfully.
meaning.zh: 诸葛亮借东风帮助火攻；比喻巧妙利用有利时机和条件。

equivalents: take advantage of the right moment

examples.zh: 这次新品上市赶上了节日热潮，真是诸葛亮借东风。
examples.en: The product launch caught the holiday rush, a real case of borrowing the east wind.

examples.zh: 他懂得借势营销，每次都像诸葛亮借东风。
examples.en: He knows how to ride a trend and, like Zhuge Liang, always borrows the east wind.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Zhuge Liang foresaw an east wind in winter at Red Cliff (《三国演义》 chapter 49); it was weather lore, not magic.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《三国演义》第四十九回，诸葛亮预知冬季东南风。

story.en: In the novel, Zhuge Liang builds an altar and 'borrows' a south-east wind so that Zhou Yu's fire attack on Cao Cao's fleet can succeed at Red Cliffs. The phrase is used for seizing a favourable moment. The episode is fiction, not in the histories.
story.zh: 小说中诸葛亮筑坛祭风，借来东南风助周瑜火攻曹营；后用以比喻巧借有利时机。此情节出自小说，正史无载。

date.en: late Yuan to early Ming, 14th c.

pinyin: zhāng fēi chī dòu yá —— xiǎo cài yī dié
literal: Zhang Fei · eat · bean sprouts — small · dish · one · plate

meaning.en: For the huge-eating Zhang Fei a plate of sprouts is nothing; something that is a piece of cake.
meaning.zh: 对食量惊人的张飞来说，一碟豆芽不算什么；比喻事情很容易办。

examples.zh: 这点活儿对他来说，张飞吃豆芽——小菜一碟。
examples.en: For him this bit of work is a piece of cake.

examples.zh: 别担心，修电脑我是张飞吃豆芽，小菜一碟。
examples.en: Don't worry, fixing computers is a piece of cake for me.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The humour comes from Zhang Fei's fierce, hearty image in 《三国演义》; 小菜一碟 is also a stand-alone phrase.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。幽默来自《三国演义》里张飞豪爽的形象；“小菜一碟”也可单独使用。

text: 诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡——忍痛割爱
pinyin: zhū gě liàng huī lèi zhǎn mǎ sù —— rěn tòng gē ài
literal: Zhuge Liang · wipe away tears · behead · Ma Su — bear · pain · cut off · love
natural: Zhuge Liang tearfully executes Ma Su

meaning.en: Zhuge Liang had his favoured officer Ma Su executed for losing Jieting; to give up something dear with reluctance.
meaning.zh: 街亭失守后，诸葛亮挥泪处斩爱将马谡；比喻忍着痛苦舍弃心爱的人或物。

examples.zh: 公司为了保全大局，只好诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡，裁掉了亲信。
examples.en: For the company's sake, the boss tearfully dismissed his favourite, like Zhuge Liang with Ma Su.

examples.zh: 这套收藏我只好来个诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡，忍痛卖掉了。
examples.en: I tearfully sold off this collection, like Zhuge Liang executing Ma Su.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. In 《三国演义》 chapter 96 Ma Su disobeys orders at Jieting and Zhuge Liang, bound by military law, executes him though he loves him; also a symbol of impartial discipline.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《三国演义》第九十六回，也象征执法公正。

pinyin: zhū gě liàng diào xiào —— jiǎ cí bēi
literal: Zhuge Liang · pay respects at funeral — false · mercy
natural: Zhuge Liang pays his respects at a funeral

meaning.en: Zhuge Liang weeps at Zhou Yu's funeral although he was his rival; to show pretended sympathy for someone one is glad to see fall.
meaning.zh: 诸葛亮到周瑜灵前哭祭，其实暗自高兴；比喻对失败者假装同情。

examples.zh: 对手出了丑，他还来安慰，简直是诸葛亮吊孝——假慈悲。
examples.en: His rival was disgraced and he came to console him, a case of crocodile tears.

examples.zh: 她一边说可惜，一边偷笑，真是诸葛亮吊孝。
examples.en: She said what a pity while laughing inside, a real Zhuge Liang at the funeral.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From 《三国演义》 chapter 57, where Zhuge Liang goes to mourn Zhou Yu, his rival, who died of anger. The 歇后语 is often applied to hypocrites.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《三国演义》第五十七回，诸葛亮到东吴吊唁周瑜。

text: 孙悟空翻筋斗——十万八千里
pinyin: sūn wù kōng fān jīn dǒu —— shí wàn bā qiān lǐ
variants: 孙悟空翻跟头——十万八千里
literal: Sun Wukong · turn · somersault — hundred thousand · eight thousand · li

meaning.en: One somersault of Sun Wukong's cloud covers 108,000 li; used to say that something is very far, or that two things are poles apart.
meaning.zh: 孙悟空一个筋斗云能翻十万八千里；形容相距极远，或相差极大。

examples.zh: 你这个方案和客户的要求，真是孙悟空翻筋斗——十万八千里。
examples.en: Your proposal is miles away from what the client wants.

examples.zh: 他家离公司，简直是孙悟空翻筋斗——十万八千里。
examples.en: His home is an enormous distance from the office.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The cloud somersault (筋斗云) carries 108,000 li at a time in 《西游记》; 十万八千里 is also used alone.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《西游记》，“十万八千里”也可单独使用。

text: 孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手心——枉费心机
pinyin: sūn wù kōng tiào bù chū rú lái fó de shǒu xīn —— wǎng fèi xīn jī
variants: 孙悟空逃不出如来佛的手心——枉费心机
parts: 孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手心
literal: Sun Wukong · jump · cannot · out of · Tathagata · Buddha · 's · palm — in vain · waste · mind · scheme
natural: Sun Wukong cannot jump out of the Buddha's palm

meaning.en: However clever or powerful, one cannot escape the real master's control, so all schemes are wasted.
meaning.zh: 不管多聪明厉害，也逃不出真正掌控者的手心，一切算计都是白费。

equivalents: all that scheming is in vain

examples.zh: 你想瞒过老板，孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手心，别费劲了。
examples.en: You want to fool the boss? Forget it, you're like Wukong in the Buddha's palm.

examples.zh: 他自以为聪明，其实是孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手心。
examples.en: He thinks he's clever, but he's still in the Buddha's palm.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From 《西游记》 chapter 7: Wukong bets he can leap out of the Buddha's hand, flies to the end of the world and writes on a 'pillar', but it is the Buddha's finger.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《西游记》第七回，孙悟空自以为到了天边，原来仍在如来佛手心。

text: 刘姥姥进大观园——少见多怪
pinyin: liú lǎo lao jìn dà guān yuán —— shǎo jiàn duō guài
literal: Granny Liu · enter · Grand View · Garden — see little · marvel much
natural: Granny Liu enters the Grand View Garden

meaning.en: Poor old Granny Liu's gaping at the luxury of the Jia mansion; someone who has seen little finds everything strange and astonishing.
meaning.zh: 乡下老妇刘姥姥初入贾府大观园，见什么都新奇；比喻见识少，什么都觉得奇怪。

equivalents: a country bumpkin in the big city

examples.zh: 第一次进五星级酒店，他像刘姥姥进大观园，看什么都新鲜。
examples.en: On his first visit to a five-star hotel he gaped at everything like Granny Liu.

examples.zh: 这是我第一次来国际车展，真是刘姥姥进大观园。
examples.en: It was my first international motor show, and I felt like Granny Liu in the Garden.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From 《红楼梦》 chapters 39–41. The punchline can also be 眼花缭乱 or 大开眼界, depending on the speaker.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《红楼梦》第三十九至四十一回，后半句也可说“眼花缭乱”“大开眼界”。

text: 鲁智深倒拔垂杨柳——力大无穷
pinyin: lǔ zhì shēn dào bá chuí yáng liǔ —— lì dà wú qióng
literal: Lu Zhishen · upside-down · pull up · weeping willow — strength · great · without · limit
natural: Lu Zhishen pulls up a willow

meaning.en: Lu Zhishen uprooted a willow with his bare hands; used of a person of enormous strength.
meaning.zh: 鲁智深赤手拔起垂杨柳；形容人力气极大。

examples.zh: 他一手就搬起了冰箱，真是鲁智深倒拔垂杨柳——力大无穷。
examples.en: He lifted the fridge with one hand, as strong as Lu Zhishen.

examples.zh: 别小看她，她是鲁智深倒拔垂杨柳，力气大着呢。
examples.en: Don't underestimate her; she is as strong as Lu Zhishen.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. See also the story 倒拔垂杨柳 from 《水浒传》 chapter 7.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。参见《水浒传》第七回“倒拔垂杨柳”。

pinyin: lín chōng shàng liáng shān —— bī shàng liáng shān
literal: Lin Chong · go up · Liangshan — forced · up · Liangshan

meaning.en: Lin Chong, framed and persecuted, had no choice but to join the outlaws; to be driven to extreme measures by circumstances.
meaning.zh: 林冲遭陷害，走投无路才上梁山落草；比喻被逼无奈而采取非常行动。

equivalents: have no choice but to take the plunge

examples.zh: 公司逼他降薪，他只好辞职，真是林冲上梁山。
examples.en: The company pushed him into a pay cut, and he had no choice but to resign.

examples.zh: 他被债务逼得像林冲上梁山一样，只得出走。
examples.en: Driven into a corner by debt, he had to leave.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From 《水浒传》 chapters 7–11, where the drill-master Lin Chong is framed by Gao Qiu. 逼上梁山 is also a common four-character expression.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《水浒传》林冲遭高俅陷害的情节；“逼上梁山”本身也是常见成语。

pinyin: jiǎng gān dào shū —— shàng dàng shòu piàn
literal: Jiang Gan · steal · letter — fall · trap · suffer · deception

meaning.en: Jiang Gan stole a forged letter planted by Zhou Yu and so took the bait; to be taken in by a trick.
meaning.zh: 蒋干盗走周瑜设计的假书信，中了反间计；比喻上了别人的当。

examples.zh: 他看到那封假邮件就信以为真，像蒋干盗书一样上当了。
examples.en: He took the fake email for real and fell for it, like Jiang Gan.

examples.zh: 别再蒋干盗书了，被人利用了还不知道。
examples.en: Don't be like Jiang Gan again, used without knowing it.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From 《三国演义》 chapter 45: Zhou Yu's trick makes Cao Cao execute his own naval commanders. Jiang Gan is a byword for a gullible go-between.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《三国演义》第四十五回，周瑜施反间计，曹操错杀水军将领。

meaning.en: The creation myth in which Pangu separated sky from earth; used for an unprecedented, world-changing beginning.
meaning.zh: 盘古分开天地的创世神话；比喻前所未有的开创之举。

examples.zh: 盘古开天的神话讲的是世界的由来。
examples.en: The myth of Pangu splitting heaven tells how the world began.

examples.zh: 这是盘古开天以来的头一回。
examples.en: This is the first time since Pangu split the heavens.

story.en: In the 'Records of the Three and Five', heaven and earth were once a chaos like an egg; Pangu, born in it, split them over 18,000 years.
story.zh: 《三五历纪》：“天地浑沌如鸡子，盘古生其中，万八千岁，天地开辟。”

usage.en: Often extended to 盘古开天辟地. Used for creation stories and for 'first ever' events, in a joking way.
usage.zh: 常说成“盘古开天辟地”。多用于创世故事，戏称“前所未有”。

meaning.en: The myth in which the goddess Nüwa moulded the first humans from yellow clay.
meaning.zh: 女娲用黄土捏出人类的神话。

equivalents: the creation of mankind by Nüwa

examples.zh: 小学语文课学了女娲造人的神话。
examples.en: In primary school we learned the myth of Nüwa making mankind.

examples.zh: 这幅壁画画的是女娲造人。
examples.en: The mural depicts Nüwa making mankind.

story.en: The 'Customs and Traditions' says that when heaven and earth were opened, Nüwa kneaded yellow earth to make people.
story.zh: 《风俗通义》：“俗说天地开辟，未有人民，女娲抟黄土作人。”

usage.en: A myth title used for the origin of humankind; sometimes joked about when something is lovingly handmade.
usage.zh: 神话题目，指人类的起源；有时戏称精心手作。

pinyin: sān guò jiā mén ér bù rù
literal: three · pass · home · door · yet · not · enter
natural: pass one's own door three times without going in

meaning.en: Yu the Great, busy taming the floods, passed his home three times without stopping; devotion to public duty over family.
meaning.zh: 大禹治水，三次路过家门都没进去；形容为公事忘我、不顾私家。

equivalents: pass one's own door without stopping

examples.zh: 医生们连续奋战，三过家门而不入。
examples.en: The doctors fought on day after day, passing their own doors without stopping.

examples.zh: 他为了工程项目三过家门而不入，家人都很理解。
examples.en: He passed his own door three times for the project, and his family understood.

story.en: Mencius says that Yu spent eight years away from home, passing his door three times without entering.
story.zh: 《孟子》：“禹八年于外，三过其门而不入。”

usage.en: A word of praise for self-sacrificing public servants. The classical wording is 三过其门而不入.
usage.zh: 多用于赞扬舍小家为大家的人。原文作“三过其门而不入”。

meaning.en: The legend of the divine farmer who tried herbs to learn which cured and which poisoned; the spirit of testing things on oneself.
meaning.zh: 神农亲口尝遍百草，分辨药性和毒性的传说；比喻亲身试验的精神。

examples.zh: 中医常提神农尝百草的故事。
examples.en: Traditional Chinese medicine often tells the story of Shennong tasting a hundred herbs.

examples.zh: 科学家像神农尝百草一样，亲自试用新药。
examples.en: Scientists test the new drug on themselves, like Shennong tasting herbs.

story.en: The Huainanzi says Shennong tasted the flavours of herbs and waters and met seventy poisons in one day.
story.zh: 《淮南子》：“神农……尝百草之滋味，水泉之甘苦，令民知所辟就。当此之时，一日而遇七十毒。”

usage.en: Shennong, 'the Divine Farmer', is credited with inventing agriculture and herbal medicine. Often cited when someone takes personal risks to test something.
usage.zh: 神农被视为农业和草药的发明者。常用于称赞亲身冒险试验的人。
